description: Answers 'where did that number come from?' Returns an ELC figure from the Data Points registry with its citation id, source and the date it was last verified, so an agent can quote the figure and show where it came from. An unknown id returns the three nearest ids instead of a guess.

context.description: Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."

query.description: Plain words to search the registry when you do not know the id, e.g. 'meetup attendance'.

name: cite_benchmark

data.description: Machine-readable payload; this is what `signature` covers.

signature.description: Detached JWS (RFC 7797) over the JCS-canonical form of `data`; verify against jwks_url.

source.description: Canonical engineeringleaders.io page this answer derives from.

verdict.description: Headline verdict, when the tool returns one.

title: Cite an ELC benchmark with a verifiable reference
